prompt: Activate and deactivate (toggle) qtiqmmfsrc camera streams at runtime via gst_pad_set_active — no gst_element_request_pad/release at toggle time, no camera reconfiguration, no gap on already-running streams. All three pads (1080p, 720p, 480p) are requested once at startup; link_stream/unlink_stream only call gst_pad_set_active(TRUE/FALSE) plus add/remove downstream elements (waylandsink or omxh264enc/qtic2venc + h264parse + mp4mux + filesink) without releasing the qtiqmmfsrc pad. Selectable -u Basic (default) or Full usecase; element named 'qmmf'. Use when you want gapless stream toggling without triggering a full camera reconfiguration cycle — distinguish from gst-add-remove-streams-runtime which always calls gst_element_request_pad and gst_element_release_request_pad (full add/remove lifecycle with reconfiguration) and from the bundle examples which batch multiple streams into one reconfiguration.

Full add/remove stream lifecycle on qtiqmmfsrc at runtime via gst_element_request_pad and gst_element_release_request_pad — each add/remove triggers a full camera reconfiguration on qtiqmmfsrc. Creates three streams (1080p, 720p, 480p) and adds/removes them in different orders including through PLAYING and PAUSED state transitions; element named 'qmmf'. Output: waylandsink display or omxh264enc/qtic2venc + h264parse + mp4mux + filesink. Use when you need to dynamically add and fully remove qtiqmmfsrc pads at runtime (full lifecycle) — distinguish from gst-activate-deactivate-streams-runtime which only toggles gst_pad_set_active without releasing pads (no reconfiguration), and from the bundle examples which batch multiple streams into one reconfiguration.

Bundle add/remove of multiple qtiqmmfsrc streams with a single camera reconfiguration — add a group of streams together so qtiqmmfsrc reconfigures only once for all of them. Creates stream_inf_1 (1080p) first and sets PLAYING (one reconfiguration), then transitions to READY, creates stream_inf_2 (720p) and stream_inf_3 (480p) while in READY, then transitions back to PLAYING — the two new streams are configured in a bundle (single reconfiguration) instead of per-stream. Source element named 'camerasrc'; encoder is v4l2h264enc (not omxh264enc/qtic2venc). Output: v4l2h264enc + h264parse + mp4mux + filesink or waylandsink display. Use when you want to batch-add multiple streams to minimize reconfiguration count — distinguish from gst-add-remove-streams-runtime (per-stream reconfiguration, element named 'qmmf') and from gst-activate-deactivate-streams-runtime (no reconfiguration, just pad activate/deactivate).

Plugin-examples variant of the bundle add/remove stream sample — same single-reconfiguration bundle behavior as gst-add-streams-as-bundle-example but with different encoder selection and element naming: source element named 'qmmf' (not 'camerasrc'), encoder is qtic2venc (CODEC2_ENCODE build) or omxh264enc (not v4l2h264enc). Adds stream_inf_1 (1080p) first then bundles stream_inf_2 (720p) and stream_inf_3 (480p) together in a single qtiqmmfsrc reconfiguration when transitioning PAUSED->PLAYING. Output: qtic2venc/omxh264enc + h264parse + mp4mux + filesink or waylandsink display. Use when the target board requires qtic2venc or omxh264enc instead of v4l2h264enc — structurally identical to gst-add-streams-as-bundle-example but from the plugin-examples source tree with encoder and element name differences.

12-stream multi-batch YOLOv8 detection C app using qtibatch: 12 filesrc/qtdemux/h264parse/v4l2h264dec streams fanned from one mp4-file, grouped into three 4-stream qtibatch groups each with one shared qtimltflite HTP inference graph (htp_device_id spread across two DSP cores), demuxed via qtimldemux, per-stream qtimlpostprocess(yolov8 results=10), 4x3 qtivcomposer grid, waylandsink. Programmatic stream management: set_composer_pad called after linking, static PadAddedData array. Use when you need a C app for 12-stream batch inference vs. the gst-launch batch pipeline.

Classifies audio events/sound classes from an mp4/mp3 file source or live microphone (pulsesrc) input, displaying classification labels with optional synchronized video preview via waylandsink, using the yamnet tflite model on htp/npu. Audio-only or audio+video pipeline using audioconvert/audioresample/audiobuffersplit before inference; plugins qtimlaconverter (pre-process), qtimltflite (inference), qtimlaclassification plus classification_filter (post-process).

YAMNet audio classification from an mp4-file containing H.264 video and MP3 audio, displaying classification results as a BGRA label panel overlaid on video via qtivcomposer to waylandsink. Dual qtdemux dynamic-pad blind-link: video pad to v4l2h264dec/NV12/qtivcomposer sink_0; audio pad to mpegaudioparse/mpg123audiodec/audioconvert/audioresample/audiobuffersplit/qtimlaconverter/qtimltflite(CPU delegate)/qtimlaclassification/classification_filter(BGRA)/qtivcomposer sink_1. CPU runtime (GST_ML_TFLITE_DELEGATE_NONE), no HTP/NPU. Distinct from the corpus YAMNet audio classification entry which uses HTP and FLAC file input.

Classifies objects in a live video stream from usb-camera, libcamera, mp4-file, or rtsp and overlays classification labels on display, using inception_v3 (also resnet18/101, googlenet, resnext50/101, squeezenet, wideresnet50, shufflenet-v2) tflite, dlc (SNPE), onnx, or QNN models on htp/npu (dsp delegate). Single-stream pipeline with tee-split preview/inference branches composited via qtivcomposer; plugins qtimlvconverter (pre-process), qtimlsnpe/qtimltflite/qtimlqnn/qtimlonnx (inference), qtimlvclassification plus classification_filter (post-process).

Detection-then-classification daisy chain — stage 1 detects objects with yolox on htp/npu (QNNExternalDelegate), stage 2 classifies each detected ROI crop with inception-v3 (or resnet101/resnet18/resnext50/resnext101/googlenet/squeezenet/wideresnet50/shufflenet-v2) via up to 4-way qtivsplit, results merged by qtimetamux and composited via qtivcomposer onto fpsdisplaysink. Sources: qtiqmmfsrc ISP camera, v4l2src USB camera, mp4-file, rtsp. Use when you need per-bounding-box classification labels after detection — not keypoint/skeleton pose estimation.

Detection-then-pose-estimation daisy chain — stage 1 detects persons with yolox on htp/npu, stage 2 runs hrnet_pose on detected-person ROI crops from a 2-way qtivsplit to estimate skeleton keypoints. Both stages use qtimltflite (QNNExternalDelegate); stages linked via two qtimetamux elements; final composed view via qtivcomposer onto fpsdisplaysink or waylandsink with qtivoverlay bounding-box/pose overlay. Sources: qtiqmmfsrc ISP camera, v4l2src USB camera, mp4-file, rtsp. Use when you need bounding boxes AND skeleton keypoints together in one pipeline — not per-crop classification.

Person-triggered video recording from qmmfsrc-camera/mp4-file/rtsp source to display preview plus conditional mp4-file (v4l2h264enc/mp4mux) output using a yolox object-detection model on htp/npu. Recording only starts when the detection postprocess metadata reports a human in frame; otherwise the pipeline just runs display preview via qtivcomposer/fpsdisplaysink.

Event encoder C app: conditional recording on person detection from mp4-file source with waylandsink live preview. Dual-pipeline conditional MP4 recording that starts only when YOLOX object detection metadata reports a person in frame and stops after 150 no-detection frames. Dual pipeline_main + pipeline_recoding; detection_tee splits qtimltflite (HTP external delegate) to two independent qtimlpostprocess instances: BGRA for qtivcomposer overlay display, text/x-raw for appsink metadata trigger. Event-triggered recording; qtivcomposer NV12 capsfilter (no framerate, with width/height/interlace-mode/colorimetry).

Detects faces in a live video stream from camera, mp4-file, or rtsp and overlays face bounding boxes on display, using face_det_lite (Lightweight Face Detection) tflite or QNN models on htp/npu. Single-stream pipeline with tee-split preview/inference branches composited via qtivcomposer; plugins qtimlvconverter (pre-process), qtimlqnn/qtimltflite (inference), qtimlvdetection plus detection_filter (post-process), waylandsink display.

Face detection from isp-camera (qtiqmmfsrc camera=0) live source using a QNN .bin model on the DSP backend (qtimlqnn), Topology A bounding box overlay via qtimetamux/qtivoverlay to waylandsink. ISP camera face detection with QNN engine and .bin model (not tflite). qtimlqnn loads the model with QNN HTP backend and system libraries; waylandsink sync=false for live camera. Use for face detection from the built-in ISP camera with a QNN .bin model.

Runs a daisy-chained multi-model face pipeline (face detection, then 3DMM facial-landmark mapping, then face recognition/attribute classification) on a live video stream from camera or rtsp, overlaying results on display via waylandsink, using face_det_lite, facemap_3dmm, and face_attrib_net tflite or QNN models on htp/npu. Sequential inference stages linked through qtimetamux and tee splits; plugins qtimlvconverter (pre-process), qtimltflite/qtimlqnn (inference), qtimlvdetection, qtimlvpose, and qtimlvclassification (post-process) in a batch/multi-model chain.

Single-stream three-stage face recognition C app from mp4-file to display: face detection (qfd, stage 1), facial landmark 3DMM pose estimation (lite-3dmm, stage 2), face recognition/attribute classification (qfr, stage 3). Per-stage qtimetamux, qtimltflite HTP external-delegate inference, qtivoverlay to waylandsink. Includes face_recognition.json labels and face_recognition_settings.json (confidence threshold + registered face database). 3-stage face daisy-chain: face_det_lite, facemap_3dmm, Facial-Attribute-Detection models.

Metadata parser example C app: YOLOv8 object detection with dual-branch appsink bounding box parsing from mp4-file to waylandsink display plus console bbox metadata output. detection_tee after qtimltflite (HTP) splits to two qtimlpostprocess instances: display branch (BGRA) to qtivcomposer sink_1; metadata branch (text/x-raw) to appsink with gst_value_deserialize parsing of GstStructure bounding-box label/confidence/rectangle. Topology B: no qtimetamux/qtivoverlay, appsink metadata extraction and parsing.

Metadata parsing example that counts people per frame from qmmfsrc-camera/mp4-file/rtsp source, running yolox object detection on htp/npu (qtimlsnpe/qtimltflite) and displaying overlayed boxes via qtivcomposer/fpsdisplaysink. An appsink pulls the qtimlvdetection postprocess metadata buffer-by-buffer to extract and print the live person count.

Estimates monocular depth from a live video stream from camera, mp4-file, or rtsp, displaying the original and depth-overlayed output side by side on wayland, using midasv2 (Midas-V2) tflite, dlc (SNPE), or QNN models on htp/npu. Single-stream pipeline with tee-split preview/inference branches composited via qtivcomposer; plugins qtimlvconverter (pre-process), qtimlsnpe/qtimltflite/qtimlqnn (inference), qtimlvsegmentation plus segmentation_filter (post-process).

Multi-stream multi-output object detection that scales up to 6 streams of the same input type (all camera, all mp4-file, or all rtsp) and simultaneously routes annotated output to any combination of waylandsink display grid, mp4-file filesink, and qtirtspbin RTSP server — all concurrently via an enc_tee. Grid layout auto-selects 1x1 / 2x2 / 3x3 based on stream count; qtivcomposer stitches annotated streams into the composed frame. YOLOv5 tflite-only model on QNNExternalDelegate htp/npu (qtimltflite); per-stream qtimlvconverter + qtimlpostprocess detection branches. Use when you need both a wall-display and a file recording from multiple cameras simultaneously, or when gst-ai-object-detection needs to scale beyond one stream.

Batched multi-stream inference — the only multistream app in this cluster that groups mp4-file streams into batch-size-4 batches via qtibatch so a single qtimltflite call processes all streams in one pass, then splits per-stream results with qtimldemux. File source only (up to 24 streams); no live camera or rtsp input. Supports yolov8 object detection or segmentation on htp/npu; qtivcomposer arranges outputs into 1x1/2x2/3x3/4x4/5x5 display grids or filesink. Use when you need one batched inference call across multiple file streams rather than one inference call per stream.

4-stream multistream face detection C app from mp4-file (H.265) with 2x2 qtivcomposer grid display: four independent filesrc/qtdemux/h265parse/v4l2h265dec decode chains fanned from one mp4 file, per-stream tee, qtimlvconverter, qtimltflite HTP external-delegate inference on face_det_lite (qfd module), Topology A overlay via qtimetamux/qtivoverlay, dedicated qtivcomposer sink pad per stream, waylandsink fullscreen.

2-stream multistream face recognition C app: two parallel three-stage face recognition daisy-chains (qfd -> lite-3dmm -> qfr) on two independent filesrc/qtdemux/h264parse/v4l2h264dec mp4-file streams, composited side-by-side via qtivcomposer to waylandsink. Per-stage qtimetamux; qtimltflite HTP external-delegate on face_det_lite, facemap_3dmm, Facial-Attribute-Detection models. Multi-stream parallel face recognition: two simultaneous face recognition pipelines in one process.

Per-stream multi-source AI inference across up to 32 camera (qtiqmmfsrc/qmmfsrc), mp4-file, or rtsp streams — the only multistream AI app in this cluster that accepts live ISP camera and rtsp as well as file inputs, and runs one independent qtimltflite inference branch per stream (no batching via qtibatch). Supports yolox detection or inception-v3 classification on htp/npu (QNNExternalDelegate); can mix detection and classification in a single run. qtivcomposer composes overlaid streams into 2x2 up to 6x6 display grids; output to waylandsink display, mp4-file, or rtsp server.

Single-stream object detection app — detects objects and draws bounding boxes — supporting every source (mp4-file filesrc, ISP camera qtiqmmfsrc, USB camera v4l2src NV12/YUY2/MJPEG, libcamera, RTSP rtspsrc) and every output (waylandsink display, mp4-file filesink, RTSP server qtirtspbin). Also the correct starting point for two-stream and three-stream detection requests when no dedicated multi-stream C app exists in the corpus. Supports yolov5/yolov7/yolov8/yolox/yolonas models in tflite, SNPE dlc, QNN, and ONNX formats on htp/npu. Tee-split preview and inference branches composited via qtivcomposer with side-by-side composition support; qtimlvconverter, qtimltflite/qtimlsnpe/qtimlqnn/qtimlonnx inference, qtimlpostprocess bbox overlay, ISP camera and file encode to mp4.

Parallel multi-task inference on one qmmfsrc-camera/mp4-file/rtsp stream to display using object detection (yolox), classification (inception-v3), pose estimation (hrnet), and image segmentation (deeplabv3-plus-mobilenet) run simultaneously on htp/npu. Four independent qtimltflite branches process the same tee'd source and are composited as a 2x2 matrix via qtivcomposer onto fpsdisplaysink, each accelerated by QNNExternalDelegate backend_type=htp.

Detects human pose keypoints in a live video stream from camera, usb-camera, mp4-file, or rtsp, overlaying skeleton/joint labels on display (or streaming out via RTP/file), using hrnet_pose (HRNetPose) tflite or QNN models on htp/npu. Single-stream pipeline with tee-split preview/inference branches composited via qtivcomposer; plugins qtimlvconverter (pre-process), qtimltflite/qtimlqnn (inference), qtimlvpose plus pose_filter (post-process).

Performs semantic segmentation on a live video stream from camera, mp4-file, or rtsp and overlays per-pixel segment labels on display, using deeplabv3_plus_mobilenet (DeepLabV3) or FFNet-40S/54S/78S tflite, dlc (SNPE), or QNN models on htp/npu. Single-stream pipeline with tee-split preview/inference branches composited via qtivcomposer; plugins qtimlvconverter (pre-process), qtimlsnpe/qtimltflite/qtimlqnn (inference), qtimlvsegmentation plus segmentation_filter (post-process).

AI-driven smart codec pipeline for bandwidth savings and storage reduction — ISP camera (qtiqmmfsrc) source ONLY, not usable with file or USB inputs. Runs YOLOv8 tflite object detection on htp/npu to steer qtismartvencbin adaptive bitrate encoder: qtismartvencbin receives three inputs from qtiqmmfsrc — full-res NV12_Q08C main video on sink, 640x480 preview on sink_ctrl, and text/x-raw detection metadata on sink_ml. Reduces bandwidth by cutting bitrate in static/background regions and allocating more bits to AI-detected ROI. Output: v4l2h264enc, h264parse, mp4mux, filesink mp4. Use when the encode source is an ISP camera and the goal is AI-steered adaptive bitrate — compare with gst-qimsdk-smartcodec-mp4-display for mp4-file source.

Upscales/enhances an mp4-file video stream via super resolution and shows the original and upscaled output side by side on display, or muxes the composited result to an mp4 file, using quicksrnetsmall (QuickSRNet small/medium/large, XLSR) tflite models on htp/npu. Single-stream pipeline with tee-split original/inference branches composited via qtivcomposer; plugins qtimlvconverter (pre-process), qtimltflite (inference), qtimlvsuperresolution (post-process), with v4l2h264enc/h264parse/mp4mux/filesink for file output or fpsdisplaysink for display.

USB-camera-only object detection and preview app — the only detection app in this cluster where the only input source is v4l2src (UVC USB camera); no ISP camera (qtiqmmfsrc), no file, no RTSP input. Two distinct modes: a no-ML preview mode (display / filesink / RTSP with YUY2/NV12/MJPEG USB formats) and a detection mode with optional YOLOv5/YOLOv7/YOLOv8/YOLOX/YOLONAS detection overlaid on live USB preview. Output: waylandsink display, mp4-file (v4l2h264enc + mp4mux), or qtirtspbin RTSP server. Use this when the only available capture device is a USB UVC webcam.

Image classification from an mp4-file video source to a display, appsink, or encoded video file using a quantized ResNet101 TfLite model on htp/npu via the QNN external delegate. Video-stream preprocess with qtimlvconverter, inference with qtimltflite, postprocess with qtimlpostprocess (module=mobilenet-softmax, imagenet labels, confidence threshold) overlaid via qtimetamux/qtivoverlay onto the decoded video.

Mp4-file-only detection-then-pose daisy chain with runtime-configurable gst_parse_launch pipeline string (--source/--output flags) — the only daisy-chain app in this cluster built on a dynamic launch string rather than hardcoded element links, and the only one with mp4-file as the default/only supported source. Output selectable at runtime: waylandsink display, v4l2h264enc mp4-file encode, or appsink raw frames. Uses yolox/yolov8-postprocess detection and hrnet pose models on QNNExternalDelegate htp/npu; qtimlpostprocess merges detection+pose metadata before qtivoverlay.

Minimal mp4-file-only object detection app using gst_parse_launch pipeline string construction (not manual element linking). Source is always mp4-file (filesrc/qtdemux/h264parse/v4l2h264dec); output is selectable at runtime via --output flag: waylandsink display, encoded mp4-file, or appsink for raw frame capture. Uses YOLOX tflite on QNNExternalDelegate htp/npu with qtimetamux + qtivoverlay for bounding-box overlay (not qtivcomposer). Designed as an educational/lightweight starting point — simpler than gst-ai-object-detection, no camera support, no RTSP, no SNPE/QNN/ONNX model variants.

Video-stream preprocess and inference only, from an mp4-file source to a raw tensor dump via appsink, using a quantized ResNeXt101 TfLite model on htp/npu via the QNN external delegate. Demonstrates qtimlvconverter for tensor conversion feeding qtimltflite inference, writing inference output buffers to a file for further processing without any postprocess/overlay stage.

Video-stream preprocess, inference, and postprocess pipeline from an mp4-file source to JSON results via appsink, using a quantized ResNeXt101 TfLite classification model on htp/npu via the QNN external delegate. qtimlvconverter preprocesses, qtimltflite runs inference, qtimlpostprocess (module=mobilenet-softmax, imagenet labels) applies classification postprocess, and qtimlmetaparser converts results to JSON output.

Video-stream preprocess only, from an mp4-file source to an inference-ready tensor dumped via appsink to a file. Demonstrates qtimlvconverter converting decoded NV12 video frames into INT8 neural-network tensors (no crop, no inference, no postprocess) for downstream processing.

Video-stream crop and preprocess, from an mp4-file source to an inference-ready tensor dumped via appsink to a file. Demonstrates qtivtransform cropping a region of interest from the decoded video followed by qtimlvconverter producing INT8 tensors for inference, with no model/inference or postprocess stage.

Semantic segmentation from an mp4-file video source to a display, appsink, or encoded video file using a quantized DeepLabv3+ mobilenet TfLite model on htp/npu via the QNN external delegate. Video-stream preprocess with qtimlvconverter, inference with qtimltflite, postprocess with qtimlpostprocess (module=deeplab-argmax), then qtivcomposer alpha-blends the segmentation mask over the decoded video frame.

Minimal isp-camera (qtiqmmfsrc) to single appsink pattern — the simplest appsink reference in this cluster, built entirely with gst_parse_launch. qtiqmmfsrc feeds a queue then a single appsink with new-sample signal and pull-sample callback; no dual sinks, no YUV stride/offset metadata extraction, no mp4 decode. Use as the minimal baseline for pulling raw ISP camera buffers into a C application via appsink.

Dual parallel appsink from isp-camera (qtiqmmfsrc) — the only appsink app in this cluster with two simultaneous sinks: one raw appsink (saves /data/frame_n.raw) and one YUV appsink (saves /data/frame_n.yuv) with GstVideoMeta stride/offset retrieval (vmeta->stride[0], vmeta->offset[1]/vmeta->stride[0]). ISP camera source only; demonstrates simultaneous multi-sink camera buffer capture and YUV plane layout inspection. Use when you need both raw and YUV camera buffers saved in parallel.

Hotplug detection via qtiqmmfsrc device-status-change GObject signal — the only camera app in this cluster that listens on the GStreamer plugin's native signal to detect when the secondary POV camera is physically attached or detached at runtime, auto-switching between BWC-only, POV-only, and BWC+POV pipeline states. Two independent qtiqmmfsrc pipelines (built-in BWC + POV camera) each built via gst_parse_launch. Interactive text menu: turn cameras on/off, switch to POV/BWC, edit pipelines live, capture images. Use when hotplug should be detected through the GStreamer plugin signal (not GPIO).

ISP camera image-quality tuning demo — the only camera app in this cluster dedicated to enabling/disabling SHDR (staggered HDR), LDC (lens distortion correction), and EIS (electronic image stabilization) as sensor/ISP flags on qtiqmmfsrc, piped through capsfilter to waylandsink. No encoding, no AI, no hotplug, no camera switching. Pipeline: qtiqmmfsrc -> capsfilter -> waylandsink. Use when you need to test HDR, lens distortion correction, or electronic image stabilization sensor modes on an ISP camera.

Runtime camera swap between two ISP cameras every 5 seconds without stopping the pipeline — the only camera app in this cluster that alternates between camsrc_0 (camera0) and camsrc_1 (camera1) in PLAYING state via live pad relinking. No hotplug event detection, no ISP tuning flags. Output: waylandsink display preview (-d flag) or v4l2h264enc/h264parse/mp4mux mp4-file encode (default). Use when you need to cycle between two ISP cameras on a fixed interval without a pipeline restart.

Builds a single pipeline capturing from qtiqmmfsrc camera, encoding to H.264 with a runtime-selectable encoder (qtic2venc default, or v4l2h264enc with DMABUF io-mode) through h264parse (config-interval=1), then streams live via qtirtspbin RTSP server instead of file or display output. Reference for exposing a qtiqmmfsrc camera capture as an rtsp stream with selectable encoder/QP/bitrate properties rather than writing to an mp4-file or waylandsink display.

Two concurrent ISP cameras (qtiqmmfsrc) recording simultaneously, no AI and no display — the only multistream app in this cluster that starts two independent qtiqmmfsrc pipelines (camera1, camera2) in parallel within the same process, each encoding via qtic2venc/h264parse/mp4mux to its own mp4-file filesink with per-pipeline GMainLoop bus and error handling. No object detection, no video wall grid, no display output. Use when you need two ISP cameras recording to separate files at the same time without inference.

Programmatic (non-gst_parse_launch) single-stream object detection using the qtimlvideotflitebin high-level inference bin — the only app in this cluster that wraps pre-process + tflite inference + postprocess into a single qtimlvideotflitebin element with qtivoverlay for bounding-box overlay. Source is mp4-file only (filesrc/qtdemux/h264parse/v4l2h264dec). Uses YOLOv8 tflite on QNNExternalDelegate htp/npu; output is always waylandsink display. Educational reference for explicit element-by-element C pipeline construction and dynamic-pad connection pattern with verbose comments.

GBM-backed appsrc buffer source — the only transform app in this cluster where the pipeline source is a GstAppSrc pushing application-allocated GBM buffers (video/x-raw(memory:GBM)) from raw NV12 YUV frames read from a file on disk, using a custom GstBufferPool (gst_gbm_qdata). Downstream tee splits to qtic2venc/omxh264enc encode-to-mp4mux-filesink and waylandsink display simultaneously for zero-copy dmabuf-style buffer supply. No camera element, no qtivtransform rotate/flip/scale. Use when the source is the application itself supplying pre-allocated GBM buffers.

Multi-stage AI vision pipeline for real-time hand gesture recognition, accepting usb-camera, isp/htp camera, rtsp, or mp4-file input and running chained qtimltflite inference stages (palm_detection.tflite, hand_landmark.tflite, gesture_embedder + canned_gesture_classifier tflite models) with qtimetamux metadata fusion and qtivoverlay detection overlay rendering. Demonstrates a tee-based multi-branch pipeline supporting selectable output-type of none, file (mp4), rtsp (rtspclientsink), or webrtc (webrtcbin with SDP/ICE negotiation) alongside optional waylandsink display, combining camera/network input, on-device AI inference, and flexible streaming/display output.

Hotplug detection via GPIO edge interrupt — the only camera app in this cluster that triggers on a physical hardware GPIO input pin (/dev/gpiochip0, line offset 42) rather than qtiqmmfsrc's device-status-change GObject signal. Same dual-pipeline BWC+POV architecture as gst-camera-hotplug-example but wired to GPIO for embedded/automotive use where the attach event comes from a hardware pin. Two independent qtiqmmfsrc pipelines; interactive text menu with same controls. Use when POV camera hotplug must be detected via GPIO edge-triggered input rather than GStreamer plugin signal.

General-purpose security/IP camera monitoring application performing YOLOv8 object detection on any input source type — the broadest input coverage in the cluster: usb-camera (v4l2src), ISP camera (qtiqmmfsrc), rtsp (rtspsrc), or mp4-file — and the broadest output coverage: display (waylandsink), mp4-file (v4l2h264enc/mp4mux), rtsp (qtirtspbin), or webrtc (webrtcbin with WebSocket signalling). Programmatic (non-gst_parse_launch) pipeline explicitly built element-by-element in C. Uses yolov8_det_quantized.tflite on QNNExternalDelegate htp/npu; qtimetamux + qtivoverlay for bounding-box overlay. Use when you need both RTSP or WebRTC output and flexible source selection in a security camera scenario.

PPE (personal protective equipment) compliance monitoring app — the only two-stage sequential detection pipeline in this cluster. Stage 1 runs foot_track_net_quantized.tflite (person/feet detection) on htp/npu; Stage 2 runs gear_guard_net.tflite (helmet/vest PPE detection) on htp/npu. Both models run qtimltflite + qtimlpostprocess. Input: usb-camera (v4l2src), ISP camera (qtiqmmfsrc), rtsp, or mp4-file. Output: display, mp4-file, rtsp, or webrtc. Programmatic explicit C pipeline; detects whether workers are wearing safety gear (hard hat, safety vest). Use when the task is PPE compliance, safety gear detection, construction-site monitoring, or worker protection.

Event-triggered recording from an mp4-file to display and a conditional mp4-file output using a yolov8/yolox tflite model on htp/npu; recording pipeline starts when a person is detected and stops after 150 consecutive no-person frames. Dual-pipeline design: main pipeline uses filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec, qtimlvconverter, qtimltflite, qtimlpostprocess (yolov8), qtivcomposer, fpsdisplaysink; secondary recording pipeline is appsrc-fed and uses v4l2h264enc, mp4mux, filesink, triggered and stopped from an appsink detection callback.

Smart codec pipeline for bandwidth savings from mp4-file source ONLY (not a camera) — the only smartcodec-with-AI app in this cluster that reads from filesrc instead of qtiqmmfsrc. Runs YOLOv8 tflite detection on QNNExternalDelegate htp/npu and feeds detection metadata to qtismartvencbin for AI-driven adaptive bitrate encoding. Three-pad qtismartvencbin wiring: sink (main NV12 decode output), sink_ctrl (640x480 qtivtransform downscale for scene analysis), sink_ml (text/x-raw detection metadata via tee_meta). Encoder constructed with gst_element_factory_make_with_properties (encoder=2, v4l2h264enc) at construction time, not post-hoc. min-buffers=1 required for file sources. Simultaneously displays annotated video with qtimetamux + qtivoverlay + waylandsink. Compare with gst-ai-smartcodec-example for ISP camera source.

Restricted zone / geofence violation monitoring app — the only detection app in this cluster whose domain is spatial zone compliance rather than generic object detection. Detects people's feet using foot_track_net_quantized.tflite on QNNExternalDelegate htp/npu, evaluates foot position against a predefined restricted area, and flags zone violations with overlay annotations. Input: usb-camera (v4l2src), ISP camera (qtiqmmfsrc), rtsp, or mp4-file. Output: display, mp4-file, rtsp, or webrtc. Programmatic explicit C pipeline (not gst_parse_launch). Use when the task is perimeter monitoring, zone intrusion detection, or geofence enforcement rather than generic bounding-box detection.

Camera-only smart codec bandwidth reduction without AI — the only transform app in this cluster that uses qtismartvencbin for content-aware adaptive bitrate from an ISP camera (qtiqmmfsrc) source with no AI model and no htp/npu inference. qtiqmmfsrc feeds two pads: main NV12 stream to qtismartvencbin sink, low-res preview to qtismartvencbin sink_ctrl; no sink_ml. Uses smart-framerate, smart-gop, and scene-complexity-based bitrate control. Output: v4l2h264enc, h264parse, mp4mux, filesink. Camera source only — compare with gst-transform-example for rotate/flip/scale and gst-ai-smartcodec-example for AI-steered camera smart codec.

Rotate, flip, and scale via qtivtransform with simultaneous display and encode — the only transform app in this cluster that performs geometric video transforms (90/180/270 degree rotation, horizontal/vertical flip, arbitrary resolution scaling e.g. 1080p to 720p). Source is ISP camera (camera_src_bin) or H.264 mp4-file (filesrc/qtdemux/v4l2h264dec); after qtivtransform a tee splits to waylandsink display and v4l2h264enc/h264parse/mp4mux/filesink simultaneously. No AI, no appsrc/appsink, no smart codec. Use when the task is rotate, flip, scale, or orientation correction.

Plays back an mp4-file (AVC/H.264 or HEVC video, e.g. filesrc/qtdemux/h264parse or h265parse into v4l2h264dec or v4l2h265dec) to waylandsink display, driven by an interactive text menu for play, pause, fast-forward, and rewind. Demonstrates video playback trick-mode seeking (gst_element_seek with rate/GST_SEEK_FLAG, time-based and speed-based fast-forward/rewind) and pipeline state-change handling via an async message queue.

Near-duplicate variant of the interactive video playback sample for mp4-file playback to waylandsink display with a text-menu interface offering play, pause, fast-forward, and rewind controls, accepting a user-supplied gst-launch style pipeline via a -e/--source option rather than a hardcoded codec pipeline. Demonstrates video playback trick-mode seeking (time-based/speed-based rate changes) and pipeline state tracking through an async queue, from the plugin-examples source tree with minor refactoring differences (pipeline/plugins list vs pr_pipeline naming, inline formatting) from the other video-playback-example copy.

Minimal mp4-file to single appsink pipeline — the only appsink app in this cluster with an mp4-file input (filesrc/qtdemux/h264parse/v4l2h264dec NV12 decode) rather than a live ISP camera. Pulls raw decoded video frames via appsink new-sample callback; writes each frame buffer to disk. No display sink, no dual sinks, no AI, no htp/npu. Built with gst_sample_apps_utils explicit element linking. Use as the baseline for grabbing decoded mp4 file frames in C code via appsink.

Multi-stream AI video wall with multiple NPU instances — the only multistream app in this cluster that accepts 1–31 rtsp or mp4-file inputs (--input-count), runs YOLOv8 object detection across multiple htp/npu instances simultaneously (--num-npus scale-out), and composites all detection-overlaid streams into an 8x4-cell grid. Explicitly programmatic (non-gst_parse_launch) C pipeline; v4l2h264dec or rtph264depay input branches; qtivcomposer/compositor for layout. Output: display, mp4-file, rtsp, or webrtc. Use for large-scale multi-camera monitoring when you need per-stream detection distributed across multiple NPU instances.

Streams live camera video over the network via webrtc send/receive, capturing from qtiqmmfsrc, encoding with v4l2h264enc, and negotiating a peer connection through webrtcbin while registering with a websocket/soup signaling server for ID exchange. Demonstrates webrtcbin SDP offer/answer and ICE candidate exchange, rtph264pay/rtph264depay RTP framing, and receiving a remote peer's stream back into an appsrc-fed decode-and-waylandsink display pipeline for two-way video calling.

Near-duplicate variant of the webrtc send/receive video-call sample streaming live camera video via webrtc send/receive with webrtcbin, qtiqmmfsrc capture, v4l2h264enc encoding, and a websocket/soup signaling server for peer registration and ID-based connection setup. Demonstrates webrtcbin SDP negotiation, on-ice-candidate/on-negotiation-needed callbacks, and remote-stream decode plus waylandsink display, from the plugin-examples source tree with minor structural differences (single combined pipeline vs primary/secondary split) from the other webrtc-sendrecv copy.

Launches up to four independently specified GStreamer pipelines (each supplied via a repeatable --source command-line option, must include a waylandsink) so multiple video streams are composed together on-display through the weston/wayland compositor. Demonstrates weston/wayland composition of several concurrent waylandsink outputs driven from user-provided pipeline strings via gst_parse_launch, useful for multi-camera or multi-stream display layout testing.
